workflow.critical: All generated tests MUST use the project's existing test framework
Never use custom test utilities — use standard framework APIs only

step.goal: Load context and detect test framework

check.action: Scan project for test framework: - Check package.json for jest, vitest, mocha, jasmine - Check requirements.txt/pyproject.toml for pytest, unittest - Check existing test files for import patterns - Check test configuration files (jest.config, vitest.config, pytest.ini)

step.action: Identify: - Test directory structure (tests/, __tests__/, *.test.*, *.spec.*) - Existing test patterns and style - Available test utilities and helpers - Mock/stub patterns used
Ask user or auto-discover: - Specific files/modules to test - Story acceptance criteria to cover - Or: full project scan for untested code
For each target file: - Read the complete source code - Identify all exported functions/classes/components - Map dependencies and imports - Identify edge cases and error paths

For each target function/method/component: 1. Create test file following project naming convention 2. Write test setup (imports, mocks, fixtures) 3. Generate tests for: - Happy path (expected inputs → expected outputs) - Edge cases (empty, null, boundary values) - Error paths (invalid inputs, thrown exceptions) - Type validation (if applicable) 4. Use descriptive test names that explain the behavior 5. One logical assertion per test 6. Mock external dependencies, test the unit in isolation

Follow framework-specific patterns: - Jest: describe/it blocks, expect().toBe/toEqual - Vitest: same as Jest API - Pytest: test_ functions, assert statements, fixtures - Playwright: test() blocks, expect() locators

For API endpoints and service interactions: 1. Create integration test files 2. Test API request/response contracts: - Status codes (200, 201, 400, 404, 500) - Response body structure and types - Authentication/authorization enforcement - Input validation error messages 3. Test service-to-service interactions 4. Test database operations (CRUD with assertions) 5. Use test database or in-memory alternatives

check.action: For critical user journeys: 1. Create E2E test files 2. Test complete user workflows: - User registration/login flow - Primary feature workflows - Error recovery flows 3. Use semantic locators (role, label, test-id) 4. Add proper waits (waitForSelector, not sleep) 5. Keep E2E tests focused on critical paths only

step.action: Create test generation report: - Files created (with paths) - Test count by type (unit/integration/E2E) - Estimated coverage improvement - Any skipped areas with rationale
step.output:

**Tests Generated:** - Unit: {{unit_count}} tests in {{unit_files}} files - Integration: {{integration_count}} tests in {{integration_files}} files - E2E: {{e2e_count}} tests in {{e2e_files}} files
